source: Cross-check of Source/COAVamp's actual C++ headers/cpp against build notes, not a boot-test — this is a singleplayer UE5 project with no live server to boot. Re-run this diff any time a new system is built to catch drift.
caveat: "Ready to test" here means the C++ compiles clean and is ready for a real Play-In-Editor/Standalone pass — nothing below has actually been run and confirmed working in a live session yet, even the items marked ready. Status values: crit = investigated but not built, or confirmed likely broken; warn = C++ complete but needs additional in-editor work (an asset authored, a Blueprint graph rewired) before it can even be tested at all; good = compiles clean, no further C++ work needed before testing. Items with a checks list can be marked tested behavior-by-behavior — a system only shows fully tested once every one of its checks is checked.

items.name: ACOACharacterBase / ASC wiring
items.desc: Abstract base unifying ability code across ACOAPlayerCharacter and ACOAEnemyCharacter, the two sibling classes with no other common ancestor. Declares the pure-virtual GetCOAAttributeSet() every subclass implements.

checks.label: Player character's ASC resolves correctly through ACOAPlayerState in a live PIE session
Enemy character's own ASC activates abilities correctly when AI-possessed
GetCOAAttributeSet() returns the right set on both subclasses
Abilities correctly resolve the pawn via Cast<ACOACharacterBase>(GetAvatarActorFromActorInfo())

items.name: UCOAAttributeSet
items.desc: Health/MaxHealth, Blood/MaxBlood, AttackPower, StrideCharges/MaxStrideCharges. No Stamina (removed as dead/unreferenced). No XP attribute — the existing XP/Level system stays Blueprint-only by deliberate choice.

checks.label: Health decreases correctly when a DamageEffectClass GE lands
Health/Blood correctly clamp at 0 and at their Max
Blood is spent correctly by an ability's CostEffectClass
StrideCharges increases/decreases correctly through real gameplay

items.name: UCOAGameplayAbility base + native tags
items.desc: Blueprintable/BlueprintSpawnable ability base class with an AbilityID FGameplayTag. Native gameplay tags declared in COAGameplayTags.h/.cpp under the COAGameplayTags:: namespace — no Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini used, by deliberate choice.

checks.label: A subclassed ability activates correctly from its real input binding
Native tags resolve correctly at runtime (no missing-tag warnings in the log)

items.name: Crimson Resonance (channel feed/drain)
items.desc: Channel/duration ability, polls every ~0.2s via a looping timer for interrupt conditions (target dead, escaped, out of reach), cleans up active GE handles/timer on EndAbility.

checks.label: Channel starts correctly on activation
Interrupts correctly when the target dies, escapes, or leaves reach
Grants the Fed Recharge Buff correctly on a kill mid-channel (distinct from the target just escaping)
Cleans up GE handles/timer on EndAbility with no lingering state

items.name: Tail Lash (melee arc sweep + knockback)
items.desc: Instant fire-and-forget ability — calls EndAbility immediately after applying its effects, no channel needed.

checks.label: Arc sweep hits every target actually inside its range
Knockback applies correctly to hit targets
Ends immediately with no lingering state between casts

items.name: Umbral Veil (stealth)
items.desc: Grants a State.Stealthed tag (Infinite-duration, no-modifier GE) for as long as the ability owns it; breaks on movement or any other ability activating.

checks.label: Grants the stealth state tag on activation
Breaks correctly on movement
Breaks correctly the instant any other ability activates

items.name: Crimson Burst (AoE lifesteal)
items.desc: Instant fire-and-forget AoE ability with a lifesteal heal back to the caster.

checks.label: AoE correctly hits every valid target in range
Lifesteal heals the caster proportional to damage actually dealt

items.name: Umbral Chains (single-target root)
items.desc: Instant activation, delayed one-shot cleanup: zeroes the target's MaxWalkSpeed, removes the root after RootDuration via a non-looping timer built with per-activation payload state (not ability-level members, since UCOAGameplayAbility is InstancedPerActor) — a real overlapping-activation clobber bug was caught and fixed here before shipping.

checks.label: Target correctly rooted (MaxWalkSpeed zeroed) on hit
Root correctly removed after RootDuration
Two overlapping activations on different targets don't clobber each other's state (regression check for the bug already fixed once)

items.name: Crimson Harvest (corpse-feed, instant)
items.desc: Instant harvest ability with an explicit OnFeedBuffEffects extension array, applied to the caster on every successful harvest — built exactly so more buffs (like the Fed Recharge Buff) can be added in-editor with zero code changes.

checks.label: A successful harvest actually consumes/interacts with the corpse correctly
Every effect in OnFeedBuffEffects applies to the caster on a successful harvest

items.name: "Feed to death" Stride recharge buff
items.desc: Killing a Crimson Resonance channel target, or landing a Crimson Harvest, should temporarily speed up passive Stride-charge recharge. C++ side is fully complete (GrantFedRechargeBuff(), the State.FedRechargeBoost tag, ACOAPlayerState's tag-change handler resetting recharge progress) — needs 2 GameplayEffect assets authored and assigned in-editor before any of it can actually do anything yet.

checks.label: FedRechargeBuffEffectClass GE authored (Duration, Add modifier on StrideCharges, grants State.FedRechargeBoost)
That GE assigned into Crimson Resonance's FedRechargeBuffEffectClass slot
That GE added into Crimson Harvest's OnFeedBuffEffects array
StrideRechargeEffectClass's Ongoing Tag Requirement (Ignore State.FedRechargeBoost) added on UCOAClanDataAsset
Buff overrides normal recharge (no stacking) while active
Recharge progress resets only when the buff tag is REMOVED, not when it's added
A kill mid-channel triggers the buff; a target merely escaping/timing out does not

items.name: Skills (COASkillFunctionLibrary)
items.desc: Native mirror of the Blueprint-only skill system, reverse-engineered from the binary .uasset's own field names/types. Compiles; not yet wired into the real Blueprint graphs it's meant to replace.

checks.label: COASkillFunctionLibrary calls actually replace the duplicated logic in the Skills Blueprint graphs
Skill tree progress behaves identically to the old Blueprint-only version after rewiring

items.name: Inventory / Crafting / HotBar
items.desc: COAInventoryFunctionLibrary + COAHotbarFunctionLibrary, native structs/logic reverse-engineered the same way. Deliberately does NOT port AC_InventorySystem's equip/feed/interaction logic — judged too game-specific to reconstruct safely from the binary alone.

checks.label: COAInventoryFunctionLibrary wired into the real inventory Blueprint graphs
COAHotbarFunctionLibrary wired into the real hotbar Blueprint graphs
Equip/feed/interaction still functions correctly via the untouched AC_InventorySystem path after rewiring

items.name: COASaveGameSubsystem (Skyrim-style, unlimited slots)
items.desc: Full replacement for the old Blueprint save system: SaveNewSlot/OverwriteSlot/LoadSlot/DeleteSlot/GetAllSaveSlots/GetMostRecentSaveSlot/HasAnySaveSlots, scanning Saved/SaveGames/*.sav directly via IFileManager (no manifest object needed). Compiles clean; the old Blueprint system hasn't actually been replaced/rewired in the live UI yet, and only about 8 of ~20 save fields have a confirmed live data source.

checks.label: SaveNewSlot/OverwriteSlot creates a real .sav file on disk
LoadSlot round-trips CurrentMapName/PlayerLocation/PlayerRotation correctly
Health/MaxHealth/Blood/StrideCharges/MaxStrideCharges round-trip correctly through GAS attributes on load
DeleteSlot/GetAllSaveSlots/GetMostRecentSaveSlot/HasAnySaveSlots all behave correctly against real files on disk
PruneOldAutoSaves respects MaxAutoSaves without touching quicksaves/manual saves
The real WB_SavesScreen UI actually calls the new C++ functions, not the old Blueprint ones
Restoring GAS attributes on load applies through a real Instant Override GE (not yet built as of last check)

Fields with no confirmed live source (XP, Level, UnlockedAbilities, SkillTreeProgress, ResonanceOverflow, AbsorbedMemories, quest/world state) are either wired to a real system now or intentionally left at defaults

items.name: COALoadingScreenSubsystem + native Slate widget
items.desc: Hooks the engine's global PreLoadMap/PostLoadMapWithWorld delegates via MoviePlayer, so any Open Level travel gets the loading-screen treatment automatically, no per-caller rewiring needed. Two real bugs already found and fixed in this build (a garbage-collection crash on the background texture, and a stuck-until-click auto-dismiss bug) — highest execution-risk system in the project, and NOT yet re-tested since the second fix landed.

checks.label: Loading screen shows on a normal Open Level travel (main menu Start, save-then-load)
Auto-dismisses on its own with no click needed (regression check for the fixed stuck-until-click bug)
No repeat of the background-texture GC crash across several level transitions in a row
Splash shows only on the very first level load of the session, not on later transitions
MinimumSplashDisplayTime holds its full duration even on a fast/instant boot load
BackgroundTextures array actually picks a random Altheria concept-art panel each load
Verified in Standalone Game specifically, not just embedded PIE (MoviePlayer often doesn't render in PIE at all)

items.name: Basic melee combo pipeline
items.desc: BP_ThirdPersonCharacter's stock "Variant_Combat" template melee combo (ComboAttack/bSaveAttack/ComboIndex, bound to IA_ComboAttack). None of ACOACharacterBase/ACOAPlayerCharacter/ACOAEnemyCharacter reference Damage/Damageable/Attacker at all, meaning this combo's damage most likely never touches UCOAAttributeSet::Health or GAS at all — could not confirm live-but-broken vs. fully dead from source alone. Deliberately held off porting until this can be confirmed in a live session.

checks.label: Confirm in a live test whether basic melee actually damages an enemy's Health at all
If broken/dead, port it into the GAS pipeline the same way the Valkory clan's Blueprint GA_Melee already does correctly
